data.long_meaning: Devmahansh is a Sanskrit name derived from two words: ‘Deva’ meaning god and ‘Mahansh’ meaning great strength. This name signifies a strong and divine being. In Hindu mythology, Devmahansh is often associated with the god Shiva, who is known for his immense power and strength. The name Devmahansh carries the meaning “God of great strength” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devmahansh usually hope their child will grow to embody god of great strength and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The God Devmahansh, also known as Dev Mahadev or Mahadev, is a major deity in Hinduism. He is the protector of the universe and the lord of mountains, particularly the Himalayas. Devmahansh is depicted as a three-headed god, with the heads representing the three primary aspects of God: creation, preservation, and destruction.

Devmahansh is also known as Shiva, and is believed to have emerged from the primal gods Brahma and Shakti. According to Hindu scripture, Shiva's third eye opened when he saw the creation of the universe, and this is one of the reasons why he is depicted with a third eye.
